requirement.name: requirement
requirement.label: Requirement

source.name: source
source.doc: Where the item's content came from — a spec section, a datasheet, a conversation. Kept out of the content hash, so correcting it never marks downstream items suspect.

note.name: note
note.doc: A free-text remark about the item's provenance, kept beside the item instead of inside its body. Kept out of the content hash.

tags.name: tags
tags.doc: Free-form labels for grouping and finding items; free-text search matches tags as well as titles. Kept out of the content hash.

owner.name: owner
owner.doc: The person responsible for this item — who a question about it goes to. Kept out of the content hash, so ownership changes never invalidate downstream work.

last_reviewed.name: last_reviewed
last_reviewed.doc: The date this item was last reviewed. Bookkeeping only: kept out of the content hash.

title.name: title
title.doc: An optional short label for tables and previews. The requirement's content is the body, not this.

status.name: status
status.doc: Lifecycle of the requirement. Only active requirements count toward coverage; draft and retired ones are excluded.

rationale.name: rationale
rationale.doc: Why this requirement exists — the reasoning behind the statement, kept separate from the statement itself.

requirement.doc: Something the design must achieve, stated as one prose body. Counts toward coverage while active; a draft or retired requirement is left out of coverage entirely.

bound.name: bound
bound.label: Bound

source.name: source
source.doc: Where the item's content came from — a spec section, a datasheet, a conversation. Kept out of the content hash, so correcting it never marks downstream items suspect.

note.name: note
note.doc: A free-text remark about the item's provenance, kept beside the item instead of inside its body. Kept out of the content hash.

tags.name: tags
tags.doc: Free-form labels for grouping and finding items; free-text search matches tags as well as titles. Kept out of the content hash.

owner.name: owner
owner.doc: The person responsible for this item — who a question about it goes to. Kept out of the content hash, so ownership changes never invalidate downstream work.

last_reviewed.name: last_reviewed
last_reviewed.doc: The date this item was last reviewed. Bookkeeping only: kept out of the content hash.

title.name: title
title.doc: An optional short label for tables and previews. The bound's content is the body, not this.

limit.name: limit
limit.doc: The numeric limit itself, parsed as a quantity with a comparison — '>= 9 V', '<= 600 mA'. Required, and it is what makes this bound checkable by other items' checks.

status.name: status
status.doc: Lifecycle of the bound. Only active bounds count toward coverage; draft and retired ones are excluded.

rationale.name: rationale
rationale.doc: Why this limit is what it is — the reasoning behind the number.

bound.doc: A numeric limit the design must respect — a voltage, a current, a tolerance. Its limit field makes it checkable by other items' checks. Counts toward coverage while active.

decision.name: decision
decision.label: Decision

source.name: source
source.doc: Where the item's content came from — a spec section, a datasheet, a conversation. Kept out of the content hash, so correcting it never marks downstream items suspect.

note.name: note
note.doc: A free-text remark about the item's provenance, kept beside the item instead of inside its body. Kept out of the content hash.

tags.name: tags
tags.doc: Free-form labels for grouping and finding items; free-text search matches tags as well as titles. Kept out of the content hash.

owner.name: owner
owner.doc: The person responsible for this item — who a question about it goes to. Kept out of the content hash, so ownership changes never invalidate downstream work.

last_reviewed.name: last_reviewed
last_reviewed.doc: The date this item was last reviewed. Bookkeeping only: kept out of the content hash.

citations.name: citations
citations.doc: External documents this item relies on. Each entry needs a path — an http(s) URL or a project-root-relative file — and may carry rev, page, section, part_number, keep_copy and an id for [[cite:]] references.

title.name: title
title.doc: What was decided, in one line. Required — every decision needs a label.

status.name: status
status.doc: Where the decision stands. Only an accepted decision counts as settled and closes coverage on what it satisfies.

rationale.name: rationale
rationale.doc: Why this decision, and why not the alternatives. Required when the decision is rejected — the reason a rejection happened is the point of recording it.

date.name: date
date.doc: When the decision was made. Kept out of the content hash, so fixing a date never marks downstream items suspect.

options.name: options
options.doc: The alternatives considered, as name / verdict / because entries. Rendered as the options-considered panel on the decision's page.

checks.name: checks
checks.doc: Numeric checks: each entry compares a value from this item's calc block against a bound's limit. A failed check here is reported as an error.

decision.doc: A design choice that was made — what was picked, why, and what it satisfies. A settled (accepted) decision closes coverage on what it satisfies; a failing check on a decision is an error.

test.name: test
test.label: Test

source.name: source
source.doc: Where the item's content came from — a spec section, a datasheet, a conversation. Kept out of the content hash, so correcting it never marks downstream items suspect.

note.name: note

tags.name: tags

owner.name: owner
owner.doc: The person responsible for this item — who a question about it goes to. Kept out of the content hash, so ownership changes never invalidate downstream work.

last_reviewed.name: last_reviewed
last_reviewed.doc: The date this item was last reviewed. Bookkeeping only: kept out of the content hash.

title.name: title
title.doc: What the test proves, in one line. Required.

status.name: status
status.doc: Result of the test. Only a passing test counts as having verified what it points at.

test.doc: A verification item that proves a requirement or bound. Its verifies links count toward coverage when the test's status is passing.

component.name: component
component.label: Component

source.name: source
source.doc: Where the item's content came from — a spec section, a datasheet, a conversation. Kept out of the content hash, so correcting it never marks downstream items suspect.

note.name: note
note.doc: A free-text remark about the item's provenance, kept beside the item instead of inside its body. Kept out of the content hash.

tags.name: tags
tags.doc: Free-form labels for grouping and finding items; free-text search matches tags as well as titles. Kept out of the content hash.

owner.name: owner
owner.doc: The person responsible for this item — who a question about it goes to. Kept out of the content hash, so ownership changes never invalidate downstream work.

last_reviewed.name: last_reviewed
last_reviewed.doc: The date this item was last reviewed. Bookkeeping only: kept out of the content hash.

citations.name: citations
citations.doc: External documents this item relies on. Each entry needs a path — an http(s) URL or a project-root-relative file — and may carry rev, page, section, part_number, keep_copy and an id for [[cite:]] references.

title.name: title
title.doc: What the component is, in one line. Required.

part_number.name: part_number
part_number.doc: The manufacturer part number. Indexed into the parts page, alongside part numbers cited inside citations entries.

refdes.name: refdes
refdes.doc: Reference designators on the board — U14, R7 — where this part is placed. Kept out of the content hash.

status.name: status
status.doc: Where the part stands in this design. Only a selected component counts as settled and closes coverage on what it satisfies; a rejected one was considered and not chosen, and never satisfies.

rationale.name: rationale
rationale.doc: Why this part, or — when an alternate link is present — what makes that alternate not a drop-in. Required whenever an alternate link exists.

checks.name: checks
checks.doc: Numeric checks: each entry compares a value from this item's calc block against a bound's limit, so a component can demonstrate compliance with a bound directly.

component.doc: A part the design uses. A selected component closes coverage on what it satisfies, and it can carry its own checks against bounds. Drop-in and alternate claims between components are made here, not facts from a parts database.

group.name: group
group.label: Group

source.name: source
source.doc: Where the item's content came from — a spec section, a datasheet, a conversation. Kept out of the content hash, so correcting it never marks downstream items suspect.

note.name: note
note.doc: A free-text remark about the item's provenance, kept beside the item instead of inside its body. Kept out of the content hash.

tags.name: tags
tags.doc: Free-form labels for grouping and finding items; free-text search matches tags as well as titles. Kept out of the content hash.

owner.name: owner
owner.doc: The person responsible for this item — who a question about it goes to. Kept out of the content hash, so ownership changes never invalidate downstream work.

last_reviewed.name: last_reviewed
last_reviewed.doc: The date this item was last reviewed. Bookkeeping only: kept out of the content hash.

title.name: title
title.doc: The name of the collection. Required — an unnamed group names nothing. Kept out of the content hash, so renaming a group never marks its members suspect.

group.doc: A named collection of items — 'the PCIe interface spec' — that names the collection without letting it stand in for its members. Members point here with part_of; a group never lists its members, never appears in coverage, and nothing may satisfy one.

log.name: log
log.label: Log entry

source.name: source
source.doc: Where the item's content came from — a spec section, a datasheet, a conversation. Kept out of the content hash, so correcting it never marks downstream items suspect.

note.name: note
note.doc: A free-text remark about the item's provenance, kept beside the item instead of inside its body. Kept out of the content hash.

tags.name: tags
tags.doc: Free-form labels for grouping and finding items; free-text search matches tags as well as titles. Kept out of the content hash.

date.name: date
date.doc: When this entry was written. Required — an undated log entry cannot be ordered in time.

summary.name: summary
summary.doc: One-line account of what happened, shown in log listings above the body.

log.doc: A dated entry in the design log — work done, questions raised, corrections. Entries are append-only: each is sealed on the first build where it has no errors, and after that editing it is a build error — corrections are new entries with amends.

refines.name: refines
refines.label: Refines
refines.doc: A narrower, more detailed version of the same kind of statement: a requirement refining a requirement, or a bound refining a bound. Same category of thing, different altitude.

derives_from.name: derives_from
derives_from.label: Derives from
derives_from.doc: A bound whose value follows from a requirement or another bound — where the number came from, not a restatement of it.

governed_by.name: governed_by
governed_by.label: Governed by
governed_by.doc: This requirement must comply with a general rule stated elsewhere — another requirement or a bound — without being a narrower version of it. Traceability only; it never feeds coverage.

satisfies.name: satisfies
satisfies.label: Satisfies
satisfies.doc: A decision or component claims to meet a requirement or bound. This is the link that closes coverage once the claiming item reaches a satisfying status.

constrained_by.name: constrained_by
constrained_by.label: Constrained by
constrained_by.doc: A decision or component that must respect a bound. Traceability only — it does not close coverage on the bound; satisfies does.

verifies.name: verifies
verifies.label: Verifies
verifies.doc: A test proves a requirement or bound. Counts toward coverage when the test's status is one of the type's verifying_statuses.

addresses.name: addresses
addresses.label: Addresses
addresses.doc: A log entry records work done on a requirement or bound. Counts as addressed coverage — someone has worked on it and written it up — without claiming it is met.

records.name: records
records.label: Records
records.doc: A log entry records a decision — the design-log side of the decision's own recorded_by end of the same edge.

amends.name: amends
amends.label: Amends
amends.doc: A log entry corrects an earlier log entry. Entries are append-only, so a correction is written as a new entry pointing back at this one rather than as an edit.

supersedes.name: supersedes
supersedes.label: Supersedes
supersedes.doc: This decision replaces an older one. The older decision keeps its history; moving its status to superseded is your edit, not something the link does by itself. Because the two are separate claims, a build warns when this link says superseded and the target's status says something else.

selects.name: selects
selects.label: Selects
selects.doc: A decision picks a component. The component's own status marks it selected; this link records which decision made the pick. A build warns when either half is missing and the other is not.

blocked_by.name: blocked_by
blocked_by.label: Blocked by
blocked_by.doc: Something is holding this decision up. Name only the immediate blocker; reports resolve the chain to its root. May point at an item of any type; a cycle is a build error.

part_of.name: part_of
part_of.label: Part of
part_of.doc: This item belongs to a group. Membership is always declared by the member, never by the group; contains is the computed backlink.

drop_in.name: drop_in
drop_in.label: Drop-in
drop_in.doc: This component is a drop-in second source for that one — interchangeable as claimed, no review needed. Self-inverse, and restricted to component-to-component. For a part that is close but needs checking before it goes in a design, use alternate.

alternate.name: alternate
alternate.label: Alternate
alternate.doc: This component is functionally close to that one but not a drop-in: check before substituting. Self-inverse, component-to-component, and the rationale explaining what differs is required.
